rounding_convention: decimal.Decimal only, ROUND_HALF_UP. Money exact to the cent; EPS (basic, each tentative diluted, final diluted) rounded to 2 decimals for reporting; earnings per incremental share rounded to 4 decimals for reporting. Ranking and dilutive/antidilutive tests use the unrounded exact quotients, not the rounded display values.

journal_entries.description: Issuance of 4,000 shares of 5% cumulative convertible preferred stock, $100 par, at par
Issuance of $500,000 face, 4% Series X convertible bonds at par
Annual 5% preferred dividend declared and paid in cash the same day (4,000 sh x $100 par x 5%)
Full-year cash interest on Series X convertible bonds ($500,000 x 4%); bonds issued at par so no amortization

notes: Ranking most dilutive to least dilutive (earnings per incremental share): Employee stock options ($0.0000) < Series X convertible bonds (4%) ($1.2000) < 5% cumulative convertible preferred stock ($1.6667) < Series Y convertible bonds (10%) ($9.3750). Sequential schedule results: Employee stock options: dilutive; Series X convertible bonds (4%): dilutive; 5% cumulative convertible preferred stock: dilutive; Series Y convertible bonds (10%): antidilutive. Series Y is antidilutive because adding $22,500 after-tax interest for only 2,400 shares raises EPS above the running $1.72, so it is excluded. Options carry no numerator effect (treasury stock method: $200,000 proceeds buy 5,000 shares at the $40 average price, leaving 5,000 incremental shares). The preferred dividend is added back without a tax effect; bond interest is added back net of the 25% tax. Note the near-tie in the schedule: tentative EPS after Series X is 1.724138 and after the preferred is 1.721133 - both display as $1.72, but the exact comparison makes the preferred dilutive; final diluted EPS is $1.72 under either treatment.
